questions.question: What do you do first to compare the length of two bars?
options: Put both ends on the same line
See which one reaches the far end
Pick the one that looks wider
Count the dots on each bar
questions.explain: You put both starts on the same line first. That way you can see which one really goes farther. Just looking at which one is wider or which one reaches a spot is not the fair way.

questions.question: Two bars start at the same line. The red one ends first, and the blue one ends farther. Which is longer?
options: The red one, it looks wider
The blue one, it goes past
They look the same length
The red one, it starts first
questions.explain: Both bars start at the same line, so the one that goes farther is longer. Picking the wider one or the one that starts first is not the right way to compare.

questions.question: Anna puts one end of her ribbon and one end of her belt on the edge of her desk. The belt goes past the ribbon. What can she say?
options: The ribbon is longer, it is wider
The belt is shorter, it touches the edge
The belt is longer than the ribbon
They are the same length
questions.explain: Both ends start at the same desk edge, so the one that goes farther is longer. Saying the wider one is longer or the one that touches the edge is shorter is not the right way.

questions.question: Ben wants to compare a crayon and a marker. What is the right way to do it?
options: Count the colours on each one
See which one reaches the far spot
Pick the one that looks thicker
Put both tips on the same line
questions.explain: You put both tips on the same starting line so the comparison is fair. Just seeing which one reaches farther or picking the thicker one will not give a fair answer.

questions.question: Mia lines up a pencil and a ruler at the same edge of her paper. The ruler ends 8 cm past the pencil. What does that mean?
options: The ruler is longer than the pencil
They are the same length
The ruler is shorter, it reaches farther
The pencil is longer, it is thinner
questions.explain: Both start at the same edge, so the one that ends farther is longer. The ruler ends 8 cm past the pencil, so the ruler is longer. Picking the thinner one or the one that reaches farther is not the right idea.

questions.question: Sam holds a thick crayon and a thin crayon, both starting at the same line. The thin one goes farther, but Sam says the thick one is longer. What is his mistake?
options: He did not line up the starts
He compared width, not length
He did not count the dots right
He used the wrong colour crayon
questions.explain: Sam is looking at how wide the crayon is, not how far it goes. To compare length, you look at which one goes farther from the same starting line.

questions.question: Mia lines up two bars at the same line. The first goes to the 6th dot, and the second goes 3 dots farther. Which bar is longer?
options: The first one, it looks wider
They look the same length
The second one, it goes farther
The first one, it starts on the left
questions.explain: Both bars start at the same line, so the one that goes farther is longer. The second bar goes 3 dots past the first, so it is longer. Picking the wider one or the one on the left is not the right way.

questions.question: Tom puts a stick at the left edge of his desk and a ruler at the right edge. The ruler looks longer. Can Tom be sure it is really longer?
options: Yes, the ruler is wider than the stick
No, a ruler is too short to compare
Yes, the ruler reaches the right edge
No, they do not start at the same line
questions.explain: The stick starts at the left edge and the ruler starts at the right edge, so they do not share a starting line. Without the same starting line, you cannot tell which is really longer. Width and which edge they touch do not matter.

questions.question: Leo says, 'The thick pencil is longer than the thin pencil.' Both start at the same line, and the thin one goes farther. What went wrong with Leo's answer?
options: He is comparing width, not length
He counted the dots on the pencils
He used the wrong type of pencil
He did not line up the starts first
questions.explain: Leo is looking at how thick the pencil is, not how far it goes from the starting line. To compare length, you see which one goes farther from the same start. The thin one goes farther, so it is the longer one.

questions.question: Two bars sit on a line with both left ends touching it. Bar A ends at 5 and Bar B ends at 9. Which is longer?
options: Bar A is longer
Bar B is longer
Both are equal
You cannot say
questions.explain: When both bars start at the same line, the one that ends farther is longer. You do not need to pick them up to compare.

questions.question: You put both left ends of two pencils at the edge of your paper. Pencil 1 goes to 7 and Pencil 2 goes to 3. Which is shorter?
options: The first one
The thick one
The second one
You cannot tell
questions.explain: Both pencils start at the same edge, so the one that ends sooner is shorter. The wide one is not the short one.

questions.question: Two bars start at the same line. One ends at 12 and the other at 8. What do you check to find the longer one?
options: The wider bar
The bar colour
The top bar
The far end
questions.explain: After lining up the starts, you look at which end goes farther. Width, colour, and position do not change length.

questions.question: Bar A goes from 0 to 8 and Bar B goes from 2 to 9. A kid says Bar B is longer. What is the mistake?
options: Starts not same
Counted the dots
Held one higher
Picked the wide one
questions.explain: Bar B only looks longer because it starts at 2 instead of 0. To compare fairly, both left ends must be on the same line.

questions.question: You put two bars at the same left line and both end at 10. Your friend says the blue one is longer because it is fatter. Is that right?
options: Yes, fatter wins
No, same length
No, count the dots
Yes, starts first
questions.explain: Both bars end at 10, so they are the same length. Being fatter is about width, not length.

questions.question: You put a stick at the left edge of the table and it goes to 6. Your friend holds a stick in the air and it looks like it reaches 7. Can you compare them fairly?
options: Yes, higher one
Yes, fatter one
No, line them up
No, count the dots
questions.explain: You can only compare fairly when both sticks start on the same line. A stick in the air has a different starting point.
